description: Observable research strategies, not inferred personality traits; multiple modes can occur in one investigation.

codes.label: Procedural baseline
codes.definition: Applies repeatable known checks or a prepared playbook without a documented conceptual change.
codes.interpretation: Routine method is not a failure and a finding is not proof of novel reasoning.

codes.label: Systematic exploration
codes.definition: Maps inputs, APIs, configurations, states or reachable surfaces by a defined coverage strategy.
codes.interpretation: Breadth/coverage is distinct from conceptual originality.

codes.label: Variant reasoning
codes.definition: Transfers a previously documented failure mechanism to analogous components, versions or products.
codes.interpretation: A new vulnerability may follow an established reasoning pattern.

codes.label: Hypothesis discrimination
codes.definition: Runs a discriminating test between candidate explanations and updates beliefs from the observed result.
codes.interpretation: A negative result may still be informative.

codes.label: Anomaly-driven investigation
codes.definition: Treats unexpected observations as clues and tests alternative explanations.
codes.interpretation: Accidental discovery is not necessarily an absence of reasoning.

codes.label: Foundational assumption challenge
codes.definition: Names a previously accepted invariant and tests where it might break.
codes.interpretation: Record what was assumed, why, and the precise boundary of the challenge.

codes.label: Boundary and authority reasoning
codes.definition: Examines differences between caller, actor, tenant, trust, authority and authorization contexts.
codes.interpretation: An ordinary boundary checklist is not automatically novel.

codes.label: Time, state and ordering reasoning
codes.definition: Studies transitions, races, stale assumptions and time-dependent checks.
codes.interpretation: Preserve exact observation/occurrence chronology when available.

codes.label: Cross-domain analogy
codes.definition: Applies an explanatory structure from one technical domain to another.
codes.interpretation: Distinguish analogical transfer from actual discovered equivalence.

codes.label: Mechanism recombination
codes.definition: Connects independently known behaviors or partial capabilities to form a new testable hypothesis.
codes.interpretation: A novel chain may combine already-known mechanisms.

codes.label: Constraint reframing
codes.definition: Reformulates a blocked research question by changing an assumption or target criterion.
codes.interpretation: Do not mistake relaxed success conditions for newly demonstrated access.

codes.label: Failure-informed pivot
codes.definition: Changes direction because a failed or inconclusive attempt reduces the value of the previous path.
codes.interpretation: Document why a direction stopped, not only the new direction.

codes.label: Root cause abstraction
codes.definition: Generalizes a demonstrated failure to the mechanism or invariant that made it possible.
codes.interpretation: Avoid presenting broad patterns as fact without representative evidence.

codes.label: Tool-assisted probing
codes.definition: Uses instrumentation, code search, fuzzing or automation to collect test evidence.
codes.interpretation: Tool use does not by itself imply original insight.

codes.label: Evidence-driven prioritization
codes.definition: Chooses among research questions according to uncertainty, feasibility, expected impact or available resources.
codes.interpretation: Do not infer private intent from observed execution ordering.

novelty_levels.meaning: Uses a previously known routine or checklist.
Changes the application of a known method to fit this context.
Combines known methods to form a distinct research move.
Potentially original line of thought within reviewed prior art; not a claim of first-ever originality.

attribution_types.meaning: Source records the researcher's own stated reasoning.
Source records what they did, not what they privately thought.
A separate, unverified reconstruction of why that action occurred.

invariants: Mindset is a label for an evidenced decision/action, never an enduring researcher personality or intelligence score.
A zero-day label is an independently curated outcome variable, not a proxy for novelty.
Association does not prove a mindset caused a finding; retrospective reporting and publication bias must be tested.
Routine and original reasoning can coexist in one research trajectory and a single step can carry multiple observations.
Novelty must be assessed relative to a declared prior-art corpus and temporal cutoff, not through rhetorical confidence.
Counterfactual, reconstructed and analyst-inferred mindsets are excluded from historical summaries.
Unsuccessful and undisclosed studies are needed before comparing outcome frequencies.
